messages:
mira: quick heads-up, landed a v3-adapt kernel flip in the nightly pool and noticed tail latency drift on high-seq paged workloads. want to sync on kernel chooser and batching heuristics before wider rollout.

leo: saw the same on the 8xA100 canary. p95 up ~10-15% at seq=2048 for paged-attn flows. throughput also regressed under latency-priority batching.

toni: is it KV churn? memory thrash? or pure matmul slowdown?

kai: I ran a quick flame: matmul variants account for most extra cycles. excerpt from perf: 
```
# sample flame summary (canary-2025-10-31)
v3_adapt_matmul     48.7%\nbatcher_spinwait    14.2%\nv3_merge_kv         9.6%\nmemcpy               5.1%\nothers              22.4%\n```
We picked kernel v3_adapt_multi for heads=16, seq=2048. v2_fused-dot was faster in earlier runs.

mira: thanks. that suggests chooser picked v3 but launcher performance here is worse. bench runs?

bench-bot: bench summary link: /mnt/artifacts/bench/2515/v3-adapt-smoke.tar.gz

nina: batcher logs show it reduced target batch size after seeing higher per-request latency, which then decreased throughput. our controller currently treats kernel choice as opaque.

leo: proposal: expose per-kernel latency priors (static + online probe) to the batcher so decisions consider chosen kernel latency. add periodic micro-probing so priors stay fresh.

toni: agree. also want a short-circuit fallback in routing: if route p95 > threshold, route traffic to fallback kernel (v2_fused-dot) for N minutes. implement in routing-policy engine.

mira: rollout plan suggestion: feature-flag off by default. enable for 3% of non-paged in-memory traffic in staging, run perf/quality evals, then step to 15% canary, 50% long soak, then ramp. keep paged-attn separate until kernels tuned.

kai: test matrix I'm going to run: seq=[512,1024,2048], heads=[8,16], batch-policy=[latency, throughput], kv=[lru,ttl], path=[paged,non-paged]. will include long convo KV reuse tests to stress eviction.

mira: nice. also add a microbench on tiled matmul params to see if kernel launcher tiling choices cause regressions on 8xA100 vs 4xH100.

bench-bot: quick note: the nightly regression run that triggered alert was on 8xA100. 4xH100 preliminary microbench shows smaller delta.

nina: action items draft:
- kai/leo: post per-kernel flamegraphs + traces for failing runs (due EOD)
- mira: draft FF rollout + canary ramp + gating thresholds (p95 delta, throughput drop %)
- toni: sketch batcher change to accept per-kernel latency priors + probe scheduler by tomorrow
- leo: implement routing-policy quick-fallback prototype (30m) in staging
- ops-bot: reserve canary capacity and tag nodes for kernel experiments

ops-bot: canary pool reserved: 10 nodes tagged (kern:v3-adapt) — disk and gpu health OK.

mira: question: do we want v3-adapt enabled for non-paged only initially? paged path memory access pattern probably needs separate tuning.

toni: strongly prefer non-paged first. paged-attn introduces IO-bound components that interact with kernel merges differently.

leo: one more mitigation: batcher should back off more conservatively when it sees a kernel-specific slowdown; instead of shrinking batch immediately, probe alternate kernel in parallel for a short window before full rollback.

mira: good idea. that'll avoid thrash. add probe logic: sample 1% of requests to alternate kernel and compare latency over rolling window.

bench-bot: perf test command used by leo: 
```
./tools/attn_bench --model=GPT2-XL --gpus=8 --seq=2048 --policy=latency --kernel=auto --trace
```
logs: /mnt/artifacts/bench/2515/attn_trace.tar.gz

kai: I'll run tiled-matmul sweep tomorrow and post results here.

mira: meeting? let's do a short sync after traces posted.

ops-bot: meeting scheduled: "kernel-adapt canary sync" 2025-11-04 15:30 UTC

mira: thanks all, will follow up with a concise plan doc after the microbench results. :thumbsup:
